Heads up — I opened #46109, which builds on your feature here, rebased onto current `dev`. The idea and original implementation are yours; credit's in the PR.

One difference worth flagging back to you: on a long orchestration session we ended up with hundreds of subagent sessions, and listing all of them made the sidebar unusable. So #46109 lists only *active* subagents and dedupes by child session id (so a resumed task doesn't double-render). If you revisit this PR, that filter is probably the useful bit to lift — please take it with credit to you, no ownership claimed on my side.

Not trying to jump ahead of your PR; opened mine because our fork needed it on current `dev`. If yours lands, I'll close mine.

That capture matches the mechanism exactly — four writes of byte-identical bytes, one per subsequent part mutation. The payload isn't growing, it's being re-serialized in full every time any part of the message changes, so cost scales with (diff size × remaining mutations in the turn) rather than with the edit.

Our numbers for comparison, from a 51.3 GB database: `event` was 43.96 GB of it across 3.1M rows, and a single long-running session accounted for 17.33 GB. Same shape as yours at a different scale.

#42771 is open and fixes this. Patch text moves to a `message_diff` side table, the event payload keeps only `{file, additions, deletions, status}` metadata (~120 B/entry), and clients fetch patches lazily on expansion via a `message.diff.updated` nudge. Measured across 1,066 sampled events after the change: diff-carrying `message.updated.1` dropped from ~432.7 KB to ~4.4 KB average, peak 60 MB → 2.3 MB. It also adds an opt-in `retention.event_idle_days` sweeper for the accumulated stock, since eviction only stops new growth.

For the immediate problem on your box, while that sits: `event` rows are replay/streaming state, not durable content — `message` and `part` hold what the client actually reads. We archived ours to compressed JSONL, reset the table, and then had to `VACUUM INTO` a fresh file to actually reclaim the space, because SQLite doesn't return freed pages to the filesystem (our file was 391,355 extents; the vacuum took it to 995). Verify against your own reader set before deleting anything — that ordering is what made 45.5 GB come back rather than just becoming free pages inside a still-51 GB file.

The event-loop starvation you saw on the headless server is worth its own note on #33356 — a 29 MB single event is a serialization stall, not just disk.

Sorry for the slow reply — and the answer changed while it sat: #38955 was closed by the inactivity bot on Aug 26 (older than a month, fewer than two reactions). That's not a maintainer decision on the approach, but it does mean there's nothing to fold into. Open your own PR.

Your scope is also broader than mine was, so I don't think it wants to be the same PR anyway. #38955 was a prompt *facade* — read prompt state, edit text, drive the cursor, draw extmarks, and survive the remount problem (the prompt remounts on session switch, so a plugin holding a ref from load time has a destroyed controller; the ref lives on a context and `api.prompt.ref()` reads the live one). What it deliberately did not provide is any contract for multiple plugins transforming the same prompt: no ordering, no coalescing, no atomic commit. Yours is that missing layer.

Two things from my branch that might save you time, both lifetime-related rather than ordering-related:

- Guarded accessors (`packages/tui/src/prompt/display.ts`) — extmark calls no-op against a destroyed renderable instead of throwing, because a stale ref is the normal case, not the exceptional one.
- `offsetToScreen` returns `null` when the prompt is unmounted or not yet laid out, so overlay positioning gets an explicit "cannot answer" rather than a plausible wrong coordinate.

Branch is `iceteaSA:tui-prompt-facade` if any of it is useful — take it with no attribution needed. I'll review yours when it's up.

> Adding my use case: I have sessions with 200+ messages doing complex multi-step work (UI polish, bug fixes, markdown rendering for a survey app). After a few days, the session list is just opaque IDs — I waste time opening each one to figure out what it was about. A `/rename` slash command or `session rename <id> <name>` CLI command would make session recovery after restart much more practical.

I vote for `opencode session rename <id> <name>` I think this is absolutely necessary to organize better the work and simply "tell any model to rename current session" not just being so lazy of doing it by myself but specially when you're running opencode inside `tmux` or `herdr` and want to rename both tmux/herdr tabs and opencode session at once, just as claude code does it


As a temporary workaround, the attached `export-ai-sessions.sh` script can rename an OpenCode session directly in the local SQLite store (as well as export opencode/claude sessions):

```bash
./export-ai-sessions.sh \
  --rename-session <SESSION_ID> \
  --title "New session title"
````

[export-ai-sessions.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31596271/export-ai-sessions.sh)

Steps:
1. Find the ID of the active, top-level OpenCode session.
2. Run the command above with the desired title.
3. The script validates the session ID, rejects invalid titles, waits up to five seconds for the SQLite lock, and updates the title in a transaction.
Important: run this command from the active session itself. Do not delegate it to a subagent, because OpenCode creates a separate child session for that subagent; renaming that child changes the wrong session.
A native CLI command such as opencode session rename <id> <title> would make this workflow supported and remove the need to update the local store directly.

Confirming the plugin-side symptom from @herjarsa/omo-meta-governor@0.38.4 (V2 plugin registered in \opencode.json\'s \plugin\ array).

Reproduction:
- CLI (\opencode\ TUI or \opencode run\): all \omo_*\ tools register, all hooks fire. Verified locally on Windows 11 + bun 1.3.14.
- OpenCode Desktop (spawns \opencode serve\ in HTTP/sidecar mode): zero \omo_*\ tools in the session, hooks never fire. Plugin module-loads (we see \[meta-governor] v0.38.2 MetaGovernor plugin loaded\ in \meta-governor.log\ from the module-scope \logToFile\ call) but \createMetaGovernorPlugin(...).server(input)\ is never invoked.

This is independent of \omo-meta-governor\ itself — we shipped 4 v0.38.x releases assuming the plugin was loading in Desktop and only learned otherwise when users reported missing tools. So we have a concrete user-visible regression class that maps cleanly to \Plugin.service\ never being materialised in serve mode.

@brad07 is right that \Closes #38470\ looks wrong (the original bug is MCP-server-tools-in-via-API, different subsystem). The plugin fix stands on its own — just needs to be unlinked from #38470 so it can merge and we can declare \peerDependencies\ floor on OpenCode Desktop with confidence.

Happy to ship a regression test in \omo-meta-governor\ that exercises the serve-mode init sequence against a mocked \Plugin.service\ and fails when \plugin.server(input)\ is not called — that would document the contract from downstream's perspective. Filed #42280 as the canonical tracking issue if it's helpful for cross-reference.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #40955: Queued messages are silently dropped when a turn is interrupted — same symptom (user message persisted but session never processes it, no reply, no abort event), just triggered via Esc/abort rather than via a question-tool prompt. The root cause described there (loop not restarted after cancellation) may cover this case too.
- #43376: TUI hangs after a multi-question prompt — related question-tool deadlock scenario.

**Attribution update — confirmed opencode-side, not the driver/UI layer.** The session was driven through Tether (a web PTY client), and its journal shows the full picture:

- `14:26:29` — an earlier interrupt was handled cleanly: `turn.error "Aborted"` -> `outcome: cancelled` (durationMs 128168), followed by a normal 7ms turn. **The ordinary abort/interrupt path works.**
- `14:28:25` — the user's message ("So?") was submitted; Tether logged `turn.start` for it (the engine was handed the message).
- After `14:28:25` — **no `turn.end` ever fires**. The opencode `serve` process for this session (started 14:24) is **still alive and hung >30 min later** (verified via ps). It is not a crash and not a client kill — the process is blocked.
- The message exists in opencode's own SQLite `message` table with a `text` part and **no parentID** (submitted as a fresh user message, not as an inline answer to the prompt).

So the engine accepted the message (persisted it) but the session loop never picked it up: the loop is blocked awaiting the `question` tool's resolution and a concurrently-arriving user message neither resolves it nor queues a follow-up turn. Repro: run a task that ends in a `question` tool call, then submit a new message (don't answer the prompt inline) -> engine hangs forever, message unprocessed.

Thanks for the related-PR pointers. I reviewed #10123, #43713, and #14393 against this diff to be precise about overlap:

**This PR is a bug fix, not a config feature.**
The auto-compaction trigger in `prompt.ts` (the `Layer.effect` overflow block) passes only `lastFinished.tokens` (a single message) to `isOverflow`. For large-context models like `opencode-go/hy3`, `usable(model) = context - maxOutput = 256000 - 64000 = 192000`, but one assistant message is only ~20k tokens, so the check is always false and compaction never fires. This PR accumulates the **cumulative** token count of the whole context and passes that to `isOverflow` (which itself is untouched). No new config is added.

**Overlap check:**
- **#14393** (thinking-block signatures + overflow headroom) — orthogonal. It edits `overflow.ts`/`message-v2.ts`; this PR does not touch `overflow.ts`.
- **#10123** (custom thresholds + `min_messages`) — same function, different lines (it adds `messagesSinceSummary > minMessages` near the `result === "compact"` branch / line ~521). No identical-line conflict, but both edit the trigger region, so a rebase may be needed if it lands first.
- **#43713** (per-model compaction config) — **overlaps the exact same block**: it changes `auto: true` → `auto: model.compaction?.auto ?? true` inside the `if (lastFinished && isOverflow(...))` trigger that this PR also restructures. So this diff will require a rebase against #43713 if that PR merges first. The logic (cumulative count → `isOverflow`) remains valid regardless.

Confirmed on latest release 1.18.25 (2026-08-28), provider kimi-for-coding, model k3 (attachment: false via models.dev).

Repro: agent generated a 608 KB PDF via headless Chrome, then called `read` on it. Tool output was just "PDF read successfully", but the tool part stored `attachments[0].url = data:application/pdf;base64,...` From the next turn on, every request fails with `AI_APICallError` 400 "Invalid request Error".

Beyond the capability-check bug itself, the recovery UX is a dead end:
- retry / "continue" re-send the poisoned history → same 400;
- /compact also requires a model call with the same history → same 400;
- UI revert only offers user messages as restore points, so a mid-session tool part cannot be removed without reverting the entire session.

The only recovery was manual surgery on `opencode.db`: deleting the read tool-part and the trailing error messages. Consider (a) degrading tool-result media to a text note for attachment:false models, and (b) a way to drop a poisonous part without a model call (e.g. "retry without this attachment").

#43877 is related but not a duplicate — it's a different failure mode with a different fix:

- #43877 fails with `exitCode=1` and a `ChildProcess.spawn` error: the gc process never starts, so no repack temp files are produced (the bloat there is loose objects that gc never gets to prune).
- This issue fails with `exitCode=128` and `fatal: unable to read <sha>` / `failed to run repack`: gc runs and dies on objects the project's own `git gc` pruned from the shared object database (via the `seed()` alternates). Each failed repack leaves a `tmp_pack_*` behind — 699 files / 61.7GB on my machine.

PR #46037 addresses this issue's mode: prune stale `tmp_pack_*` after every gc run (success or failure) and rebuild the snapshot store when gc fails on missing objects. It intentionally does not fire on the spawn-error case — there the store is not corrupted, so deleting it would be wrong.

Related context from the missing-objects failure mode: PR #46037 adds cleanup that prunes stale `tmp_pack_*` files after every snapshot gc run (success or failure) and rebuilds the snapshot store when gc fails on missing objects. It doesn't target the spawn failure described here, but the tmp_pack pruning covers the disk-bloat consequence for any cleanup failure mode. For the captured-context hypothesis: on current dev the periodic loop and the event-driven path use the same `git` helper, building spawn options fresh on every call — so if that was the cause in 1.18.15, it may already be addressed upstream.


The workaround is to expose only the default plugin factory. A fix for this is now available in PR #46037: it prunes stale `tmp_pack_*` files after every snapshot gc run (success or failure) and rebuilds the snapshot store when gc fails on missing objects (the deterministic `unable to read` mode when the project's own gc prunes shared objects). Can we extract and build a smaller piece of this? I think there's a significant gain available from a small implementation focused on server plugin -> client plugin communication channel.

Server-side plugins can receive events, but they can't emit any to clients. That gap forces all client/server plugin pair into various hacks. As an example, I recently [built a plugin](https://github.com/acramsay/dotfiles/blob/main/home/.config/opencode/plugins/models-md.ts) for personal use that supplements an AGENTS.md with additional model-specific instructions. In order to make the [TUI component](https://github.com/acramsay/dotfiles/blob/main/home/.config/opencode/plugins/models-md-tui.tsx) functional, the server plugin had to spin up an additional local HTTP server (on a randomly assigned port) and write a pid file under ~/.local/state/opencode/ so the TUI plugin can discover the correct port needed to communicate with the correct http server. The workaround works, but it's far from an ideal implementation. I believe #5305 was attempting to address this same problem for a different reason.

A minimal fix is to allow server plugins to publish arbitrary event types like `plugin.<pluginID>.example` on the existing bus, and let TUI plugins subscribe with api.event.on("plugin.<pluginID>.example"). Since TUI plugins can already render Solid components via slots, this one change unblocks most "custom UI for the TUI" cases without waiting on the full client/render registry question.
